reason: The regular Israelite people are portrayed unfavorably in this passage. They are depicted as quarrelsome (ויָּרֶב הָעָם עִם־ מֹשֶׁה - 'the people contended with Moses'), ungrateful despite divine provision, and as testing God's faith (נַסֹּתָ֤ם אֶת־ יְהוָה - 'testing the LORD'). Their complaints about being brought out of Egypt to die of thirst, along with their children and livestock, are presented as expressions of doubt and faithlessness. The location is even named Massah and Meribah (מַסָּה וּמְרִיבָה) commemorating their 'testing' and 'striving/quarreling' against God, further emphasizing the negative characterization of their behavior and attitude.
